answer: Charge a falcon bridge toll before any agent crosses from the idle pool into paid work. First, each agent posts one refundable toll to cross. Second, a rotating squad of falcon checkers swoops on random crossings and re-verifies the work record behind each toll. Third, a fake caught at the nadir of activity, when it expects no watchers, loses its toll and its crossing record is burned, so it pays again to re-enter. Assumed here, each fake costs about $4,000 to field, so 1,000 fakes cost about $4 million before earning. A toll bridge keeps honest traffic moving and prices fakes out.
